q: It’s been a while since I had a problem with something I bought. How long do I have to file a consumer complaint?
evidence: shall not admit a complaint unless it is filed within two years from the date on which

q: My consumer case is worth more than ₹10 crore. Which Commission should hear it?
evidence: complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds rupees ten crore

q: The District Commission decided against me. Can I appeal, and how soon do I need to do it?
evidence: on the grounds of facts or law within a period of forty-five days from the date of the order

q: A company is ignoring an order from the Consumer Commission. What could happen to it?
evidence: imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one month, but which may extend to three years

q: A company ran an ad that misled customers. What penalty could it face?
evidence: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years and with fine which may extend to ten lakh rupees

q: I bought something for my small business. Does that make me a consumer under the Act?
evidence: does not include a person who obtains such goods for resale or for any commercial purpose

q: What makes an advertisement count as misleading under the Act?
evidence: gives a false guarantee to, or is likely to mislead the consumers as to the nature, substance, quantity or quality

q: How does the Act define a defect in goods?
evidence: any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard which is required to be maintained

q: What does e-commerce mean under this Act?
evidence: buying or selling of goods or services including digital products over digital or electronic network

q: After I file a complaint, how many days does the Commission normally take to decide whether to accept it?
evidence: shall ordinarily be decided within twenty-one days from the date on which the complaint was filed

q: How long should the Commission take to decide my complaint once the other side has been notified?
evidence: decide the complaint within a period of three months from the date of receipt of notice by opposite party

q: Up to what value of goods or services can the District Commission hear a complaint?
evidence: where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed one crore rupees

q: If both sides want to try mediation, how soon must they give their written consent?
evidence: give in writing, within five days, consent to have their dispute settled by mediation

q: I modified a product myself and it harmed me. Can I bring a product liability case against the seller?
evidence: cannot be brought against the product seller if, at the time of harm, the product was misused, altered, or modified

q: A shop shared my personal details that I gave in confidence. Is that allowed?
evidence: disclosing to other person any personal information given in confidence by the consumer
